description:
**A fill that is not a colour is still a fill.** Upstream does no parsing: whatever the encode produced lands on the scene item and goes to the renderer as it stands, so `fill: 0.28` is written into the SVG as `fill="0.28"`. This engine parsed the value, found no colour, and recorded that the mark had **no fill at all** — which is a different thing from having one that paints nothing, and upstream keeps them apart. The way in is ordinary rather than exotic: a `{"scheme": {"signal": "…"}}` whose signal has not been answered leaves the scale with d3's default `[0, 1]` range — see `a-scale-with-no-range-keeps-its-default` — so every mark keyed to it is filled with a **number**, and a palette picker starts there.

**Nothing visible turns on it, and that is worth stating rather than leaving to be rediscovered.** An unparseable presentation attribute is treated as *not specified*, so `fill` takes its inherited value — and vega's root group is `<g fill="none" stroke-miterlimit="4" …>`, so the mark paints nothing. This engine writes `fill="none"` and paints nothing too. Reasoning from SVG's *initial* value instead of its *inherited* one says black, and that reading was tried and is wrong; the group attribute is what settles it. What differed was only the record: upstream's item says a fill was asked for, and this one said none was.

Four shapes and each is load-bearing. `number` and `word` are the unparseable ones. `missing` is `{"value": null}`, which must keep recording no fill, because that is what null means and it is how a specification turns a fill off — folding it in with the unparseable ones would lose the distinction this change is about. `colour` must still parse. The **stroke** on the last rect is the other half: it was already kept, and for a second reason that does not apply to a fill — `boundStroke` asks whether an item *has* a stroke rather than what colour it is, so dropping an unreadable one left the mark a stroke-width narrower than upstream's.

**An empty value is present too, and for a stroke it is also falsey.** `blankFill` is `{"value": ""}`: upstream puts it on the item and writes `fill=""`, so it is a fill that was asked for and paints nothing, exactly as an unparseable one is. An empty **stroke** is the case this fixture cannot carry. `boundStroke` opens `if (item.stroke && …)` and `""` is falsey there, so upstream records the stroke on the item and does *not* measure it — two rects, one `stroke: ""` and one `stroke: "not a colour"`, bound 30 wide and 32. This engine can express the measuring half and not the recording half: a transparent stroke widens, because `Stroke` carries no note of the falsiness its source had, and giving it one is a field on a public class for a difference nothing can see. So the stroke stays dropped, the bounds stay right, and `an empty stroke does not widen a mark` pins it as a unit test instead. STATUS records what upstream's item holds that this one does not.
